marketRegime.rationale: US dollar strength on inflation concerns balanced by renewed geopolitical dialogue in Russia-Ukraine; energy supply risks remain but no acute systemic shocks.

executivePulse.title: Spain Labour Shock
executivePulse.text: First general strike in 14 years signals acute housing affordability crisis; labour cost pressures and political volatility ahead of elections may constrain real-estate recovery and capex deployment.

executivePulse.title: Dollar Strength & Rates
executivePulse.text: Hot inflation prints and hawkish Fed commentary lift USD; UK inflation forecast to overshoot BoE target for 4 years. Rate-sensitive sectors and EM currencies face headwinds; capital flows skew toward dollar assets.

executivePulse.title: Energy & Geopolitical Dialogue
executivePulse.text: Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchange in Abu Dhabi signals diplomatic opening; concurrent Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil hub and Iran rejection of US nuclear terms sustain Strait of Hormuz supply premium; oil prices rebound.

houseView.label: Spain & Madrid Real Estate
houseView.change: First general strike in 14 years over housing affordability signals sustained political pressure and labour cost inflation. Housing crisis now a central election issue, raising policy uncertainty and near-term transaction friction.

houseView.label: European Credit & Financing
houseView.change: UK inflation forecast to overshoot BoE target for next 4 years per NIESR; dollar strength on Fed hawkishness lifts refinancing costs for EUR-denominated borrowers. RWE-KKR £12bn UK renewables deal shows selective access persists for utility-grade credit.

houseView.label: Private Capital Deployment
houseView.change: RWE-KKR £12bn UK offshore wind close and Palomma Series A (Colombia PropTech) demonstrate capital targeting infrastructure and fintech; ICG warning over AI direct deals flags overheating in high-valuation segments. Deployment remains execution-dependent and sector-selective.

houseView.label: Energy & Commodities
houseView.change: Ukrainian drone strike on Ust-Luga and Iran rejection of US nuclear terms sustain Strait of Hormuz geopolitical premium. Oil prices rebound. Siemens Energy record orders and dividend tripling reflect grid modernisation and gas turbine demand. Supply risks support near-term pricing.

houseView.label: Emerging Markets
houseView.change: Moody's lifts India growth forecast to near 7% sustained rate; Palomma Series A signals LatAm fintech appetite. However, China trade surplus swells amid internal economic weakness; Bangladesh faces December political/inflation convergence. EM heterogeneity widens; selective positioning required.

houseView.label: Global Risk Appetite
houseView.change: Dollar strength and Fed hawkish messaging offset geopolitical dialogue gains (Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchange). Anthropic seeks record $88.5bn IPO valuation signals tail-risk appetite in tech; broader equity sentiment hinges on inflation trajectory and rate path clarity in next 30 days.

catalysts.title: US CPI print (inflation trend confirmation for Fed forward guidance)
ECB Speakers (rate-path signalling ahead of December decision)
US Initial Jobless Claims (labour market softness vs. Fed rate-hold debate)

globalBriefing: Spain's first general strike in 14 years over housing affordability signals acute labour cost and political volatility heading into elections, pressuring residential real-estate yields and transaction velocity in Madrid and major cities. Concurrently, USD strengthens on hawkish Fed commentary and hot inflation, compressing EM carry and elevating refinancing costs globally—UK inflation is forecast to overshoot BoE targets for four years, amplifying refinancing burden on European borrowers. Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchange talks in Abu Dhabi provide diplomatic relief, but Ukrainian drone strikes on Ust-Luga sustain Strait of Hormuz energy premium; oil prices rebound amid Iran nuclear negotiation impasse. Selective FDI into UK renewable infrastructure (RWE-KKR £12bn) demonstrates capital availability for long-duration, regulated assets, while AI valuations (Anthropic $88.5bn IPO, ICG warnings) and unicorn board expansion (1,900 companies) flag tail-risk concentration. India growth upgrade (Moody's, ~7% sustained) contrasts with China's weakening internal macro masked by tech exports, widening EM bifurcation; selective positioning favours India and Mexico nearshoring over broader EM beta.
marketOpen: Monitor USD strength and early CPI expectations ahead of today's inflation print; Spain labour market impact on wage expectations and ECB forward-guidance receptivity key to European rate trajectory; geopolitical Strait of Hormuz risks stabilizing but energy costs remain elevated.

macro.label: Macro & Central Banks
macro.description: Central bank decisions, inflation prints, GDP, yield curves, and FX

items.headline: Dollar firms as hot inflation, hawkish Fed talk lift rate-hike bets — Reuters
items.summary: Market pricing of US interest-rate hikes has increased on inflation concerns and Fed commentary. Dollar strength reflects capital flows into USD-denominated assets and safe-haven demand. Macro backdrop tilts toward higher for-longer US rates, pressuring refinancing costs globally.
items.relevance: USD strength compresses EM carry and ER valuations; elevates hedging costs for European and EM corporates.

items.headline: UK inflation to overshoot Bank of England target for next 4 years, NIESR forecasts — Reuters
items.summary: National Institute of Economic and Social Research forecasts UK CPI to remain above BoE's 2% target through 2030, signalling persistent price pressures and constrained policy flexibility. Structural wage and service-sector inflation cited.
items.relevance: Extended inflation above target weakens sterling and raises gilt yields; refinancing burden on UK borrowers and asset valuations pressured.

items.headline: Brazil central bank flags oil, El Niño, labor and FX shocks behind inflation rebound — WTVB
items.summary: Brazil's central bank identifies multiple inflation drivers—oil price pass-through, El Niño climate effects, labour cost pressure, and FX depreciation—offsetting prior disinflation. Signals higher bar for rate-cut resumption despite inflation risks.
items.relevance: BRL depreciation on Fed hawkishness and internal inflation risks; limits carry appeal and raises corporate hedging costs in LatAm region.

macro.keyTakeaway: If Fed maintains hawkish stance and hot US inflation persists, USD strength and higher global refinancing rates will constrain EM currency stability and capex appetite in Europe through Q1 2027.

geopolitics.label: Geopolitics & Security
geopolitics.description: Conflicts, alliances, sanctions, and power shifts

items.headline: Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi end with prisoner exchange agreement — Al Jazeera
items.summary: First direct talks between Russia and Ukraine since February 2022 resulted in a prisoner exchange accord brokered in the UAE capital. Signals potential de-escalation pathway and reopened diplomatic channels after prolonged direct hostility.
items.relevance: Geopolitical de-escalation narrative may ease energy supply premium; however, fragility of talks and ongoing strikes on infrastructure warrant cautious risk reduction.

items.headline: Ukrainian Drone Attack Sparks Fire at Russia's Key Baltic Oil Export Hub — OilPrice.com
items.summary: Ukrainian forces conducted drone strike on Ust-Luga, a critical Russian petroleum export terminal on the Baltic Sea. Attack follows pattern of bilateral infrastructure targeting and underscores ongoing supply-chain disruption risk despite diplomatic dialogue.
items.relevance: Persistent attacks on export infrastructure sustain Brent crude supply premium and hedging demand; offsetting geopolitical dialogue gains.

items.headline: Italy: 300+ schools evacuated after email bomb hoax; UK, Northern Ireland also report bogus alerts — BBC / Al Jazeera
items.summary: False bomb threats sent via email triggered evacuations at hundreds of Italian schools across Rome, Naples, Florence, Pisa and other cities. Concurrent unconfirmed alerts in UK and Northern Ireland. Italian PM Meloni confirmed no credible danger.
items.relevance: Cyber-hoax demonstrates disruption capability and potential for false-flag coordination across EU. Low immediate security risk but signals operational vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure alerting.

geopolitics.keyTakeaway: If Russia-Ukraine diplomatic talks sustain and build trust, oil supply risks may ease; however, continued infrastructure strikes and cyber-disruption attempts preserve elevated geopolitical risk premium on energy and defensive assets.

fdi.label: FDI & Capital Flows
fdi.description: Cross-border investments, sovereign wealth, and capital movements

items.headline: RWE, KKR finalise $16 billion investment in UK renewables — Reuters
items.summary: German utility RWE and US infrastructure investor KKR announced completion of £12 billion (approximately $16 billion USD) deployment into UK offshore wind projects, likely the largest renewable energy FDI in British history. Deployment structured as multi-tranche capex commitment.
items.relevance: Signals strong appetite for UK renewable infrastructure despite macroeconomic headwinds; demonstrates continued capital availability for long-duration, regulated-return assets. Positive signal for European energy transition capex.

items.headline: Venezuela lawmakers open crisis-hit power sector to private investment — Reuters
items.summary: Venezuelan parliament advances legislation permitting private capital participation in power generation and distribution. Move reflects state capacity constraints and need for foreign capex; signals potential opening for infrastructure investors despite wider sovereign risk.
items.relevance: Emerging markets infrastructure opportunity; however, Venezuela sovereign risk and capital controls remain material constraints. Selective risk-on positioning only.

items.headline: China-backed APEC framework promotes new financing options for digital infrastructure — The Nation (Pakistan)
items.summary: China-led Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation initiative announces new financing mechanisms for regional digital infrastructure (5G, data centres, fibre). Aims to mobilise capital outside traditional Western-led multilateral channels.
items.relevance: China-led alternative financing bypasses US restrictions and Western scrutiny; relevant for infrastructure investors tracking geopolitical capital flows and EM digital capex. Strategic competition over infrastructure finance intensifies.

fdi.keyTakeaway: If RWE-KKR model replicates across European renewables and EM infrastructure reopens to private capital (Venezuela, Vietnam rail), cross-border FDI in energy transition and digital infrastructure accelerates; geopolitical bifurcation of capital flows (US/China) widens.

critical-minerals.label: Commodities & Energy
critical-minerals.description: Oil, gas, metals, supply chains, and energy security

items.headline: EverMetal acquires UK critical metals recycler Advanced Alloys — Mining.com
items.summary: Consolidation play: EverMetal purchased Advanced Alloys, adding nickel, cobalt and specialty metals processing and recycling capabilities to its platform. Reflects supply-chain security strategy and margin expansion via circularity.
items.relevance: Vertical integration in critical minerals recycling de-risks supply and narrows spot-price sensitivity; relevant for EV battery and renewable energy supply-chain investors.

items.headline: Oil Prices Rebound as Middle East Supply Risks Persist; Iran Rejects Key U.S. Nuclear Demand — WSJ / EnergyNow.com
items.summary: Crude prices recovered on sustained geopolitical premium from Iran nuclear negotiation impasse and continued maritime threats in Strait of Hormuz. Iranian rejection of US nuclear demand cited as key signal of persisting tensions.
items.relevance: Energy cost pressures on industrial capex and transport; supports hard-commodity hedging and energy-linked infrastructure valuations.

items.headline: Siemens Energy More Than Triples Dividend After Record Year — OilPrice.com
items.summary: Siemens Energy announced proposed dividend more than tripled for FY2026 (ending 30 September) following record revenues and orders, driven by grid modernisation and gas turbine demand amid energy transition capex acceleration.
items.relevance: Strong order books for grid and power infrastructure signal sustained capex demand in energy transition; shareholder returns confirm cash generation strength in utilities sector.

critical-minerals.keyTakeaway: If energy transition infrastructure capex sustains and geopolitical energy premiums persist, critical minerals demand and pricing remain supported; recycling consolidation adds optionality but does not offset medium-term scarcity in transition metals.

real-estate.label: Real Estate & Infrastructure
real-estate.description: Institutional RE, infrastructure projects, and market trends

items.headline: Spain: Housing crisis prompts first general strike in 14 years — DW.com / Reuters / NBC News / NPR / France 24
items.summary: Spanish labour unions and workers' movements staged the country's first general strike in 14 years on Wednesday, focused on acute housing affordability crisis. Strike centres labour cost and housing supply pressures; expected to dominate upcoming electoral campaigns.
items.source: DW / Reuters / NBC News / NPR / France 24
items.relevance: Labour cost inflation and political volatility around housing supply/affordability directly constrain residential real-estate yield expansion and transaction velocity. Near-term headwinds for Madrid and Barcelona investor appetite.

items.headline: India's rich pivot to real estate after stock returns falter — The Business Times
items.summary: Emerging evidence that high-net-worth investors in India are rotating capital into real estate after disappointing equity market returns. Demand shift reflects wealth diversification and inflation hedge appetite.
items.relevance: EM real-estate demand in high-growth markets (India) sustains; however, Spain labour crisis underscores divergent regional cycles and policy risk in developed European markets.

items.headline: Vietnam Invites Japanese Institutions to Co-Design Long-Term Capital Channels for Rail and Energy — BigGo Finance
items.summary: Vietnam government and Japanese institutional investors (pension funds, development banks) announced joint initiative to structure long-term capital deployment for rail and energy infrastructure. Aims to formalize recurring investment vehicles.
items.relevance: Infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) platforms and long-duration capital matches long-term LP liability profiles; relevant for pension capital and Asian infrastructure exposure.

real-estate.keyTakeaway: If Spain labour costs and housing affordability crisis persist, European residential real-estate yields will compress and transaction activity decline; meanwhile India and Vietnam infrastructure-linked real-estate offerings attract capital rotation from developed market alternatives.

ma-growth.label: M&A & Private Capital
ma-growth.description: Deal flow, PE/VC activity, and corporate transactions

items.headline: Anthropic Seeks Record $88.5B Tied To Public Market Debut — Crunchbase News
items.summary: AI software firm Anthropic launched IPO registration seeking up to $88.5 billion in combined public offering and concurrent private placement, potentially the largest capital raise tied to a public market debut. Signals tail-risk appetite in AI/LLM valuations.
items.relevance: Extreme valuation multiples in AI infrastructure flag concentration risk and potential for valuation correction if adoption or monetization does not match pricing. Relevant for PE/VC allocation and tech-sector timing.

items.headline: ICG warns over direct AI deals as private equity bets big — WSJ
items.summary: Intermediate Capital Group (ICG), a major PE fund operator, issued warning about concentration of direct investments in AI companies amid heated competition for deal flow. Cautionary note on valuation discipline and downside risk in overheated segment.
items.relevance: PE cost-of-capital and deal discipline deteriorating in AI; signals potential fund-level underperformance if multiples compress or adoption slows. Risk signal for LP capital allocation into 2027 vintage funds.

items.headline: Crunchbase Unicorn Board Tops 1,900 Companies In October, 34 New Entrants, $96B Value Added — Crunchbase News
items.summary: Private-company valuations (unicorn cohort) reached record 1,900 companies in October 2026, with 34 new entrants adding $96 billion in aggregate value. Half of new unicorns under 4 years old, reflecting rapid venture-stage scaling.
items.relevance: Peak unicorn valuations and expansion of early-stage cohort (sub-4yr) suggest venture ecosystem remains buoyant but concentrated in high-growth/high-burn segments. Downside risk if capital markets access tightens or macroeconomic conditions shift.

ma-growth.keyTakeaway: If Anthropic IPO and AI-focused PE deals maintain current valuations and capital availability, venture and growth-stage M&A velocity remains high; however, ICG and market-structure warnings flag material correction risk if macro tightens or exit multiples compress.

emerging-markets.label: Emerging Markets
emerging-markets.description: Frontier opportunities, risk signals, and market access

items.headline: Moody's lifts India growth forecast, sees economy well positioned to sustain near 7% growth — Reuters
items.summary: Credit rating agency Moody's raised India's medium-term GDP growth forecast to approximately 7% annually, citing structural macro fundamentals and policy framework stability. Positions India as standout growth performer in EM cohort.
items.relevance: India macro upgrade supports equity and credit valuations; differentiates India from China (tech export boom masking internal weakness per Asia Times) and LatAm (BRL FX stress).

items.headline: China's tech export boom is hiding a weakening economy — Asia Times
items.summary: Despite swelling trade surplus driven by tech exports, China's underlying economic data signals weakness. Exports artificially inflated by reshipment and processing; domestic demand and industrial capex remain soft.
items.relevance: China macro divergence (external strength masking internal slowing) pressures CNY and increases EM contagion risk if global demand softens. Differentiates India outperformance.

items.headline: Bangladesh braces for a December of converging crises — Asia Times
items.summary: Bangladesh faces convergence of political instability, inflation, and macro headwinds in December 2026, mirroring prior-year turbulence (December 2025). Political leadership assassination context and currency pressure cited.
items.relevance: South Asia political risk (Bangladesh) and macro volatility; alongside India strength, underscores EM heterogeneity. Selective exposure required; broad EM allocations face regional concentration risk.

emerging-markets.keyTakeaway: If India sustains 7% growth momentum and China's internal weakness persists, India equity and credit outperformance continues; however, Bangladesh political risk and BRL FX stress highlight EM bifurcation—selective allocation favours South Asian growth assets over broader EM beta.

trade-policy.label: Trade & Industrial Policy
trade-policy.description: Tariffs, sanctions, export controls, and economic statecraft

items.headline: How midterm results reshape the trade landscape as tariff relief, Canada talks and USMCA review loom — Automotive News
items.summary: US midterm election results (Democratic congressional majority per prior briefing context) signal potential shift in tariff policy trajectory. Trade renegotiations (USMCA, Canada bilateral) and relief discussions now on the table; automotive sector awaits clarity.
items.relevance: USMCA renegotiation and tariff stance uncertainty create capex hesitation in North American auto and manufacturing supply chains. Policy clarity gap extends horizon for reshoring/nearshoring capex decisions.

items.headline: White House vows to press ahead with tariffs despite midterm backlash over rising prices — CNBC
items.summary: Trump administration signals continued tariff escalation despite midterm election messaging that tariffs contributed to consumer price pressures. Rhetoric suggests policy stance unshaken by electoral feedback.
items.relevance: Tariff continuation creates pricing pressure on consumer goods and industrial inputs; supply-chain costs remain elevated. Nearshoring economics more attractive if tariffs persist.

items.headline: Nearshoring Reshaping Mexico's Tech Budgets; AT&T, reshoring and what's next for US contact center operations — Mexico Business News / Channel Dive
items.summary: Nearshoring trend (Mexico, Central America) accelerates as US tariffs and labour cost arbitrage favour North American supply-chain proximity. AT&T and tech sectors cited; IT services and contact-centre labour migration observable.
items.relevance: Mexico benefits from nearshoring inflows and tariff-arbitrage demand; capex in tech infrastructure and labour retraining. Regional winner in US trade-policy bifurcation.

trade-policy.keyTakeaway: If Trump tariff regime persists despite political backlash, nearshoring to Mexico and North America accelerates, Mexico GDP and FDI benefit, but global supply-chain costs remain elevated and consumer inflation risk sustains.

food-agriculture.label: Food & Agriculture
food-agriculture.description: Food security, agribusiness, and agricultural commodities

items.headline: November WASDE Surprise: Tighter Corn and Soybean Yields, Stocks Than Expected — Successful Farming
items.summary: US Department of Agriculture's November World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates (WASDE) report surprised with tighter-than-expected corn and soybean yields and ending stocks, signalling supply constraint and potential price support.
items.relevance: Grain supply tightness supports commodity pricing and export revenues; relevant for agricultural commodity hedging and input-cost inflation in food/feed industries.

items.headline: How China's Food Security Goals Could Reshape Global Markets — Seeking Alpha
items.summary: China's strategic push for domestic food self-sufficiency (grains, proteins) aims to reduce import dependence and stabilize internal food costs. Policy shift toward domestic production incentives and strategic reserves.
items.relevance: China demand reduction for global grain imports pressures global commodity prices and EM agricultural export revenues. Strategic food security reshaping global grain trade flows.

items.headline: USDA Prepares $8 Billion Harvest Fuel Relief Payments for Farmers — Global Agriculture
items.summary: US Department of Agriculture announced $8 billion in relief payments targeting fuel costs for farmers during harvest season, offsetting energy price pressures and input inflation.
items.relevance: US agricultural subsidy support sustains farmer margins and production incentives; relevant for global supply stability and commodity pricing floor.

food-agriculture.keyTakeaway: If WASDE-indicated grain supply tightness persists and China reduces import demand, global agricultural commodity pricing remains volatile but supported; US subsidy backstop limits downside but masks structural supply constraints.
